title: Find a page in a rotated index
prompt:
A sorted list of distinct page numbers was rotated at an unknown point (for example [40, 50, 10, 20, 30]); return the index of target, or -1 if absent, in O(log n) time.

- nums has 0 to 100,000 distinct integers between -10^9 and 10^9; it may also be unrotated.
- Return a 0-based index or -1.
hints: Split the window at mid. At least one of the two halves is sorted normally. Which one?
If nums[lo] <= nums[mid], the left half lo..mid is sorted; otherwise the right half mid..hi is.
If target lies inside the sorted half's value range, search there; otherwise search the other half.

solution.explanation: After splitting at mid, the half that does not contain the rotation point is in sorted order, and nums[lo] <= nums[mid] tells you which one it is. A range check on that sorted half decides whether to keep it or discard it, so each step halves the window.

complexity.notes: Distinct values matter: with duplicates, nums[lo] == nums[mid] can hide which half is sorted and the worst case becomes O(n).

followUps: Return the rotation amount (the index of the smallest value).
How does the search change if values can repeat?
